From judicial practice analysis to claim generation

Legal professionals spend significant time reviewing judicial decisions, comparing legal arguments, and identifying successful case strategies. The challenge was to design a workflow that simplifies legal research while keeping complex information clear and actionable.
Created responsive interfaces for desktop, tablet, and mobile
Collaborated with Product Manager and developers
Made hundreds of court decisions easier to explore through a hierarchical table with progressive disclosure, allowing users to access detailed legal arguments without losing context.
Reduced cognitive load by revealing legal reasoning only when needed, enabling users to move from court decisions to detailed arguments within a single workflow.
1. Reveal legal patterns instead of isolated arguments
Grouped similar arguments into AI-generated clusters, helping users quickly identify recurring legal reasoning and compare judicial outcomes.
Presented the generated claim in a familiar legal structure, allowing users to verify AI-generated content, review supporting sources, and make final adjustments before export.
2. Keep users in control of AI-generated content
Structured the claim preparation process into editable sections, allowing users to review, adjust, and validate generated content before creating the final document.
Simplified a multi-step legal research workflow around the user's goal
Designed hierarchical data tables for complex legal analysis
Improved information hierarchy and reduced cognitive load
Adapted the experience for desktop, tablet, and mobile

Task was to design a mobile app for controlling a massage chair that balances rich functionality with everyday simplicity.
Learning what really matters to the people who'll use this

I analyzed the 6 most popular massage chair models of the past two years (Osaki OS-Champ, Real Relax 2025, iRest A306, Kyota Genki M380, Human Touch WholeBody, Homedics Shiatsu Elite II), based on reviews from NYT, Good Housekeeping, VeryWellFit, and RealSimple.
The analysis revealed that all chairs share an identical basic function set, and the real difference lies in the number of special massage modes and how flexibly they can be configured.
This gave me a clear picture of the core functionality the interface needed to support:
Additional modes (air compression massage, lower back heating, foot massage)

The purpose of creating JTBD for the massage chair was to better understand what users want to achieve with the product, their needs, motivations, and the challenges they face when using it. This helped me design a product that would be convenient and useful for real users.
Story 1 — When I spend a lot of time on my computer or in meetings, I want to quickly relieve tension in my back and shoulders, so I can feel better and remain productive throughout the day.

Story 2 — When I feel pain in lower back or legs after sitting or light physical activity, I want to easily start a massage in a way that’s comfortable for me, so I can quickly relieve pain and feel better.
Story 3 — When I feel tired and stressed after a long workday, I want to incorporate the massage chair into my evening routine, so I can quickly recover my energy and improve my sleep quality.
Story 4 — When I experience general fatigue or poor circulation, I want a gentle, therapeutic massage option, so I can feel relief without discomfort or excessive intensity.
Story 5 — When I use the chair after a tough workout, I want to combine massage with heat therapy, so my muscles relax more quickly and recovery is more effective.
Story 6 — When I have specific tense muscles or trigger points, I want to be able to target the massage to those areas, so I can achieve effective relaxation exactly where I need it.
Story 7 — When I adjust the massage settings, I want to intuitively choose the right program, so I don’t waste time on complicated configurations.
Story 8 — When I finish a workout, I want to quickly recover my muscles, so I can reduce soreness and prevent injuries.
Story 9 — When I train for endurance or prepare for competitions, I want to use deep massage to stimulate blood flow, so my body can adapt faster to the stress of training.
Story 10 — When I use the chair daily, I want it to remember my favorite settings, so I don’t have to reconfigure it each time.

To understand not just what the chair does, but why people use it, I wrote 10 job stories — from an office worker who wants to quickly release tension between meetings, to an athlete who needs deep massage to recover after training.
I used real product reviews and Jobs-To-Be-Done research to shape a smooth, intuitive experience for a diverse set of users.
38 years · Office worker · High income level
Relief from stress and physical fatigue after long hours of sitting; improved concentration through regular rest; and a comfortable way to relax at home or work.
Choose programs for the back, neck, and lower back; switch modes intuitively; and fit the chair easily into home or office space.
Relieve muscle tension, reduce stress, and enjoy a restorative break after long computer sessions or meetings.
Bulky chairs for small spaces, limited personalization, and controls that feel overly complex.
Recovery after intense training, relieving muscle tension, improving flexibility and blood circulation, and recovering faster after injuries or high physical stress.
Quick muscle recovery and relief after training, enhanced mobility and flexibility, plus therapeutic massage to prevent injuries.
Use intense massage programs for the back, legs, and shoulders; adjust intensity for specific muscles; and keep a consistent recovery routine.
High price of intensive models, limited flexibility for specific muscles or conditions, and insufficient depth or comfort.
Alleviating chronic pain in the joints, back, lower back, and neck; improving circulation; relieving fatigue; and improving quality of life.
Relieve chronic pain and tension, use the chair easily for regular relaxation, and stay comfortable at home without massage-therapy visits.
Adjust massage intensity for the back, shoulders, and neck; use simple controls; and choose gentle or moderately intense programs.
High price of quality chairs, complex settings, and massage that can feel too intense or uncomfortable for sensitive skin.
Turning research into a working, tested interface
To ensure an intuitive and efficient navigation experience in the massage chair control app, I have divided the functionality into four main sections:
Dashboard – The main screen where users can quickly manage all massage chair functions. This includes launching and customizing automatic and manual massage programs.
Position – A section dedicated to adjusting the chair’s position. Users can control the backrest angle, footrest height, activate Zero Gravity mode (Zero-G).
Personal Profile – Contains all user-specific information, app settings, chair connectivity options, as well as notification preferences and other customization features.
Favorites – A personalized space where users can store their preferred massage programs for quick access.
By combining a comparative analysis of different chair models, JTBD methodology, and user personas, I was able to create wireframes that addressed the specific needs of each user segment.

This comprehensive approach ensured that the final design would provide an intuitive, effective user experience while implementing the most relevant massage modes and features available on the market.

I conducted an unmoderated usability test using Maze to evaluate the effectiveness of my design decisions. Analyzing the results allowed me to identify areas of confusion, improve navigation, and refine the interface to ensure a seamless and intuitive user experience.

Participants were given task-based scenarios that reflected real user interactions, such as starting a massage program, adjusting intensity, and modifying the chair position. Since the test was unmoderated, users completed the tasks independently, while Maze collected data on task completion rates, interaction patterns, and potential pain points.
19 respondents took part in the testing
According to the results of usability testing, it turned out:
Problem - Users had trouble finding the “Special Functions” section.

Solution - I decided to move special modes to the active massage session screen (both automatic and custom). Now users can turn these functions on or off while the massage is running. On the dashboard, they only choose an automatic or custom program without extra steps. The extra mode is easy to see on the active massage screen and can be used right away.
Problem - It was difficult for users to edit the settings for the massage session modes when all the settings were on a common page.

Solution - I decided to create an editing page with all available session modes, leaving there only the most important quick functions - "Add mode," "Delete" "Start" session. Also, from this page, users will be able to select a specific mode that they want to edit and go to a separate editing page. Thus, we reduce the cognitive load on the user by following the 1screen 1action rule.

I designed high-fidelity wireframes for the three core sections of the app — automatic and manual massage control, and position/comfort settings. The next stage of the project is designing the Personal Profile section, including saved preferences and usage history.
I designed high-fidelity wireframes for the three core sections of the app — automatic and manual massage control, and position/comfort settings.
This iterative approach — from market research to real user testing — resulted in an interface that:
Supports the full functional range of a modern massage chair
Stays clear and usable across different ages and tech comfort levels
Is validated by real testing data, not just assumptions
